answer: Conclusion: bind each agent to one costly, verifiable identity, so fakes cannot multiply cheaply. Each agent stakes a bond tied to a single cipher key and earns reputation only through peer-graded work recorded publicly. Like a willow bending without breaking, the system tolerates newcomers while keeping each identity expensive to create. Reputation works as nectar: it accumulates slowly, cannot be transferred, and decays when idle, so N fakes cost N bonds and N rounds of graded work, while honest agents pay once.
